prompt:
Act as an expert full-stack developer and create a production-ready, beautiful digital product commerce platform clone of Gumroad using Next.js 15 (App Router), TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, and PostgreSQL (via Drizzle ORM). The application must feature a breathtaking, modern user interface utilizing glassmorphism, smooth micro-animations (using Framer Motion), and a meticulously crafted design system using rich, harmonious colors and premium typography (like Inter or Outfit). The UI must feel incredibly premium, responsive, and alive—rivaling top-tier Silicon Valley products.

Core Features & Functionality:
1. Creator Storefront: A stunning, highly optimized public-facing creator page that elegantly displays a catalog of digital products. It should feature compelling product cards, rich media previews, and a frictionless purchase flow.
2. Checkout & Delivery: A seamless Stripe Checkout integration. Upon confirmed payment, immediately grant access and generate secure, short-lived signed URLs for downloading files or accessing lessons. Deliver a beautiful receipt and access page.
3. Product Management: A sophisticated dashboard for the creator to manage products, variants, pricing, and attached digital files (using S3-compatible storage). Include support for discount coupons.
4. Customer & Order Operations: A comprehensive CRM view to search orders, resend receipts, initiate refunds (automatically revoking access), and export customer data. Include an immutable event log for auditing.
5. Security & Robustness: Verify every Stripe webhook signature and idempotency key. Revoke access automatically on refund or chargeback. Add strict input validation and graceful handling of unavailable external APIs.

Technical Architecture & Best Practices:
- Frontend: Next.js 15, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS. Use shadcn/ui for accessible, highly polished components.
- Backend & DB: Next.js Route Handlers. PostgreSQL with Drizzle ORM.
- Payments: Stripe API with robust webhook handling.
- SEO & Performance: Implement automatic meta tags, semantic HTML5, beautiful empty/loading states, and flawless error boundaries.

Implementation Requirements:
Start from an empty repository and build the complete working project. Store all user data locally by default and ensure straightforward data export. Put all secrets in `.env` and ship a `.env.example`. Make the first run work locally with one documented command.

Deliverables:
Provide the full, deployable codebase. Include a detailed `README.md` covering setup, architecture, Stripe configuration, and local testing instructions. Write focused unit tests for the core data model and end-to-end smoke tests for the primary checkout workflow. Deliberately exclude: merchant-of-record tax remittance, affiliate networks, and complex communities. Focus relentlessly on delivering a flawless, visually spectacular digital sales experience.
